description: Decision tree for execution provider selection. Used by MCP tools to recommend the appropriate EP based on hardware, model characteristics, and workflow requirements.

guidance.title: MIGraphX vs ROCm (AMD Instinct Datacenter GPUs)

MIGraphXExecutionProvider: Model operators are within MIGraphX coverage (standard CNNs, transformers with supported ops)
Workload benefits from graph-level compilation and fusion (similar role to TensorRT)
Maximum throughput is the primary goal on AMD Instinct hardware
Model uses standard ONNX operators: Conv, Gemm, Attention, LayerNormalization, MatMul
ROCMExecutionProvider: Models use custom operators not in MIGraphX operator subset
Models rely on dynamic control flow or sequence-length-dependent branching
Operators fall outside MIGraphX's supported set
Need a generic GPU fallback when MIGraphX compilation fails
Targeting consumer Radeon GPUs (RDNA architecture) where MIGraphX is not available

MIGraphXExecutionProvider: Consumer Radeon GPUs (RX 6000/7000/9000 RDNA) — MIGraphX requires Instinct CDNA hardware
Models with heavy custom operators or dynamic control flow
Platforms other than Linux x86_64 with ROCm stack
ROCMExecutionProvider: When MIGraphX is available and the model fits within its operator coverage — MIGraphX provides superior throughput via graph compilation

guidance.notes: MIGraphX provides graph-level compilation (analogous to TensorRT for NVIDIA) for maximum throughput on AMD Instinct. ROCm EP is a generic fallback that executes operators individually without whole-graph optimization. When MIGraphX encounters unsupported operators, it automatically falls back to ROCMExecutionProvider or CPUExecutionProvider for those specific ops.

guidance.title: oneDNN vs OpenVINO vs CPU (Intel CPU Inference)

OpenVINOExecutionProvider: Full Intel optimization stack is available (OpenVINO plugin installed)
Production Intel deployments requiring maximum performance
Targeting Intel iGPU, NPU, or CPU with IR-level optimizations
Need OpenVINO-specific graph transformations and layer fusion
DnnlExecutionProvider: Want lighter-weight Intel CPU optimization without installing the OpenVINO plugin
Using the default ORT wheel which bundles oneDNN (zero additional setup)
Simpler deployment without the OpenVINO dependency chain
Intel CPU with AVX2 (minimum) or AVX-512/AMX (recommended) instruction sets
Workload is CPU-bound and benefits from optimized DNNL kernels
CPUExecutionProvider: Last resort when neither OpenVINO nor oneDNN is available
Non-Intel CPUs where oneDNN provides no benefit
Maximum compatibility with no EP-specific requirements

OpenVINOExecutionProvider: When avoiding extra plugin installation is a priority
When the OpenVINO plugin is not available for the target platform
DnnlExecutionProvider: When OpenVINO is already installed and configured — OpenVINO is the preferred production choice
On non-Intel CPUs (AMD, ARM) where oneDNN provides no benefit
When using onnxruntime-gpu or platform-specific ORT builds that strip CPU-only EPs
CPUExecutionProvider: When any hardware-optimized EP (OpenVINO, oneDNN) is available — always prefer optimized EPs

guidance.notes: OpenVINO is the recommended EP for production Intel deployments (requires separate plugin install). oneDNN (DNNL) is bundled in the default onnxruntime pip wheel — zero setup, lighter-weight optimization. Use CPU EP only as a last resort. When both OpenVINO and oneDNN are detected, OpenVINO should be ranked higher in recommendations.

guidance.title: QNN Plugin vs QNN ABI (Qualcomm Snapdragon NPU)

QNNExecutionProvider: Need fine-grained multi-pass control over the optimization pipeline (OnnxConversion → quantization → QNN compilation separately)
Integrating with existing multi-step Qualcomm workflows
Troubleshooting individual pass failures in a complex pipeline
Need to apply custom quantization or preprocessing between pipeline stages
Working with models that require special handling at specific pipeline stages
QnnAbiExecutionProvider: New (greenfield) Snapdragon projects targeting Snapdragon 8 Gen 2/3+
Want single-binary deployment — model compiled directly to a context binary in one pass
Prefer simpler workflow with fewer pipeline stages
Targeting QairtPipeline for single-pass LLM quantization and compilation
Windows ARM64 for on-device NPU inference or Windows x64 for ahead-of-time context-binary preparation

QNNExecutionProvider: New projects where the simpler QairtPipeline workflow suffices
When single-binary deployment is the goal (QNN ABI is more streamlined for this)
QnnAbiExecutionProvider: Existing pipelines that rely on individual pass configuration or mixed-pass optimization
When you need to inspect or modify intermediate artifacts between pipeline stages
Legacy Snapdragon targets predating the QNN ABI runtime

guidance.notes: QNN (standard plugin) uses a multi-pass workflow: OnnxConversion → quantization → QNN compilation. This gives maximum control but more complexity. QNN ABI (QairtPipeline) compiles the model directly to a context binary in one pass — simpler workflow, preferred for fresh greenfield projects targeting Snapdragon 8 Gen 2/3+. The ABI path is newer (olive-ai 0.13.0+) and provides a more streamlined deployment experience.

guidance.title: ROCm on Consumer Radeon vs Instinct (AMD GPU Tiers)

ROCMExecutionProvider_consumer: Consumer Radeon RX 6000/7000/9000 series GPUs (RDNA architecture)
Community-maintained ROCm builds are available and working
Model fits within narrower consumer RDNA operator coverage
GPTQ quantization (preferred over AWQ on RDNA due to better compatibility)
VRAM budget of 12-16 GB (typical consumer GPU memory)
ROCMExecutionProvider_datacenter: Full vendor-supported ROCm stack is available
Broader operator coverage including MIGraphX graph compilation
Both AWQ and GPTQ quantization methods are supported
Large VRAM budgets (64-288 GB on Instinct cards)

ROCMExecutionProvider_consumer: When AWQ quantization is required — AWQ has limited support on RDNA and may produce incorrect results
Models requiring mixed-precision FP16 accumulation (unsupported on consumer RDNA)
Workloads requiring structured 2:4 sparsity (unavailable on non-CDNA architectures)
Models exceeding 7B parameters on 16 GB VRAM cards with GPTQ INT4
ROCMExecutionProvider_datacenter: Prefer MIGraphXExecutionProvider when model operators are within MIGraphX coverage — graph compilation provides superior throughput

consumer_radeon_rdna.reason: Better ROCm operator coverage on RDNA; AWQ has known compatibility gaps

instinct_cdna.reason: Full operator support on CDNA; both methods work well with MIGraphX compilation

guidance.notes: Consumer Radeon (RX 6000/7000/9000 RDNA) has limited ROCm support with community-maintained builds and narrower operator coverage. Prefer GPTQ over AWQ on RDNA due to known AWQ compatibility gaps. Instinct (MI-series CDNA) has the full vendor-supported ROCm stack, MIGraphX graph compilation, and broader operator coverage. RDNA 4 (gfx12, RX 9000 series) has experimental ROCm support status.
